summary: Vaudeville star Frank Fay pioneered solo stand-up comedy and the modern MC in 1910s-20s New York while being a violent antisemite and an abusive husband to Barbara Stanwyck; in 1946 he headlined a far-right rally at Madison Square Garden.

evidence.note: Born in San Francisco in November 1891 to traveling vaudeville performers
First prop-free solo tuxedo act around 1915 or 1916; start of main span is an estimate
Palace bookings from 1919, record runs in the mid 1920s, invents the modern MC role
Antisemitic abuse of Milton Berle and other Jewish comedians, frequent brawls
Long segment on Barbara Stanwyck's childhood and stage career before meeting Fay
Record of violent abuse of earlier wives, infidelity, drunk driving and bankruptcies
Abuse of Stanwyck and their adopted son as her film career rises; she leaves in 1935
Turns against FDR, blames Jewish bankers, befriends Father Coughlin
Pushes for investigation of anti-Franco Actors' Equity members; censured by the union
January 1946 Madison Square Garden rally organized with Klan and Nazi groups
Rally ends his career; dies in Santa Monica in 1961

notes: Primary theme is a judgement call: most airtime is his comedy career and Hollywood marriage, the fascist turn fills the last third of part 2, so fascism-far-right is secondary. Transcript spellings: Stanwick (Stanwyck), Victoria Williams (Wilson), Laura Ingles (Ingalls). Host names the American Nazi Party as a 1946 organizer, which was founded later; nazism kept for the openly Nazi rally.
